newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Views mixed on Belgian linear bonds next move.
newsitem.headline: Views mixed on Belgian linear bonds next move.

text.p: Views were mixed on Friday about the next move for the rampant Belgian linear bond market, with some traders seeing a further narrowing of the 10-year spread over German Bunds but others expecting a slight relaxation.
The spread over Bunds narrowed at one stage on Friday to a record low of eight basis points before widening again to close two points higher than Thursday at 12.
"There was a psychological barrier at eight and it held. I see the spread widening a bit from here," one trader said.
"It didn't manage to breach eight, but it will," another trader said.

Traders speculated about whether the yield on Belgian 10-year paper would fall below six percent. "It is very close now, and I think it will go through," one trader said. It was at 6.08 percent at the close, down from Thursday's 6.13 percent

"This market is absorbing bad figures without blinking. It will take a major bearish number to pull it down," he said. "Even if you are bearish on this market you have to turn around and go with it. The trend is your friend."
Traders said Generale Bank was a major buyer of 2004 and 2006 paper in the morning and was with others when bullish U.S. September payroll figures came in in the early afternoon.
Gains on the U.S. numbers pushed the spread to the record level. However, buying soon evaporated and profit-taking emerged, traders noted.
They said domestic players conducted most of the day's business.
The December bond future closed 23 basis points higher at 119.38, off an intraday high at 119.46.
